cases.note: a hot set without a window is applied, read back, and made the last change at once (§2.9, §2.6, §2.17)
a hot set the device refuses starts no change and mints no token (§2.9)

device.refused: duty cycle locked by the regulator

cases.note: a reach set: the pending reply before the apply, confirm busy until applied, then kept (§2.9, §2.10)
a reach set rolled back at its deadline: the deadline belongs to the undo (§2.11)
an undo that fails ends partial; a value not read back is unknown (§2.11)
an undo that fails, the value read back: shown as read, at runtime (§2.11)
an undo that fails, the value read back as it was before: its source from before (§2.11)
a second writer is busy; joins add groups, apply each, and are kept as one change (§2.7)
a join brings no window; a reach join that could not apply before the deadline is busy until extended (§2.7, §2.9)
extend moves the deadline from now, later or earlier, raised to the floor (§2.10)
cancel undoes now, applied or not; the last change stays (§2.10, §2.11)
a restart during a pending change rolls it back and is a new instance; a late confirm is not_found (§2.12)
persist takes the last change alone; it survives the restart, the unpersisted change does not (§2.13, §2.12)
persist refuses a change that set a sensitive value (§2.13, §2.15)
an owner with no persisted layer refuses persist unavailable, cause config (§2.13)
a retry within 300 s gets the first answer; another request under the key is refused; at 300 s it is new (§2.14)
a refusal is a first answer too; a restart forgets every key (§2.14)
a dry run answers the would-be view, and touches, mints and publishes nothing (§2.9)
one act at a time: every call is busy while an apply or an undo is in flight (§2.7)
the event's rate: a set that would start a change is busy while 600 events fall within the last hour (§2.17)
the rate spares joins, and never drops a change's event (§2.17)
a reach apply that fails ends the change at once: its applied joiners are undone (§2.9, §2.11)
a reach apply that fails with nothing else applied: rolled back with no undo act (§2.9, §2.11)
an owner starts from its persisted layer; startup is what a restart would give (§2.3, §2.12)

description: config.v1 §2.3, §2.6 to §2.14, §2.17, §2.19: sequences of calls, device results and clock instants on one owner -> its replies, its device acts, its change events and its state after each step. schemas holds the schemas by name, as in validation.json. setup: service (the owner's address), instance (its instance id; tokens are minted <instance>-<n>, n counting the instance's changes from 1, and an implementation that mints otherwise maps its tokens to these by the order it minted them), schema, startup ({group: {parameter: {value, source}}}, the startup file's or default values), overlay (the persisted layer, {group: {parameter: value}}, source overlay), floor_s, apply_after_ms (the reach apply_at the device states: the instant the set was received plus this; how a device derives it is its own), persist (whether the owner has a persisted layer), events_at (change events already published: [{t, count}], for the rate). start is the state before any step. Each step has t, seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z on the owner's clock, and do: set (group, request, call), confirm, cancel, extend or persist (request, call), due (every act owed at t: the undo when the deadline has passed, else each reach apply whose apply_at has come, earliest first), complete (the act left in flight finishes), or restart (instance: the new instance id; the persisted layer and the published events survive it). call is the O7 call metadata {actor, request_id}, or absent. device lists the results of the device acts the step makes, in order: "ok"; {"refused": words} for an apply; {"failed": words, "readback": {group: {parameter: value}}} for an undo, a parameter not in readback being unknown; "hold", which leaves the act in flight until a complete step. A missing result is "ok". expect.reply is the reply to the step's call (null for due and restart, and for a call whose act is held, whose reply comes with complete): {applied: S}, {pending: PendingReply}, {view: S}, {status: S}, each S being the status projection of the document replied (§2.19), or {refused: {code, field, cause, app}} as validation.json writes it. expect.acts lists the device acts the step started, "apply" or "undo". expect.events lists the change events published, as ConfigChangeEvent. expect.state is the owner's state after the step: status, its ConfigStatus; params, {group: {parameter: {source, startup}}} as the view shows them, each member present only when the view carries it; writable, the groups whose writable is true, in the schema's order.
